item.title: How to Crochet A Scarf In Under 3 Hours
item.description: Crochet a cozy, chunky mesh scarf perfect for summer in under three hours with this easy crochet tutorial. The scarf’s open, airy design achieves chain spaces using chunky yarn and a simple repeating pattern. Ideal for beginners, you’ll need approximately 250 meters of chunky yarn, a 9 mm crochet hook, scissors, and a large eye-darning needle. The mesh pattern gives the scarf a distinctive look and a lightweight feel. The tutor encourages customizing the width with a pattern multiple of two plus six. Finish by neatly weaving in ends for a clean look.

Como Hooded Crochet Scarf PATTERN: basic crochet stitches, video tutorial
item.description: This is crochet PATTERN ONLY. Finished scarf is NOT included Como Hooded Scarf is worked vertically (from bottom over top head and back to bottom on the other side). You start at center back. First, some increases are worked to shape the hood and at the same time the increases on both tips are worked continuously. Correct gauge is critical for exact measurements and yardages. The pattern comes in English language with US crochet terms. It contains written instructions and video tutorial. Materials: Scheepjes Woolwise (100% recycled superwash merino wool; 100g/200m) 712 Coffee Bean (or 709 Sandy Taupe) x 3 (4) 6 balls 4.5mm crochet hook Stitch markers, yarn needle Gauge: 13 sts x 12 rows to measure 10cm/4in over lemon peel stitch pattern, not stretched or blocked. Sizes: 1 (2) 3 Measurement

item.description: ✨How to work Honeycomb Stitch✨ This easy stitch pattern adds extra squish and texture to your knitting. Here’s a basic guide to working this stitch in the round. • Basic Steps: 👉 R1: *p1, s1 wyif, repeat from * to end of round 👉 R2: Knit all stitches 👉 R3: *s1 wyif, p1, repeat from * to end of round 👉 R4: Knit all stitches • Repeat R1-4 for desired length!

item.description:

Ce genre de « mitaines » donnent un peu la sensation d’un pull dans lequel on passe les pouces. ❣️ J’ai utilisé : - Une pelote acrylique - Un crochet 4mm ❣️ Les mesures : Chainette de 30ml (hauteur des mitaines), 22 rangs de mailles serrées dans le brin arrière. Rejoindre en mailles coulées (9mc) faire des mailles coulées d’un côté pour le trou du pouce (6mc) finir en rejoindre les cotés (15mc).
#loisirscreatifs #diy #doityourself...

item.title: Learn to Crochet Loop Stitch - The Easy Way
item.description: If you’ve struggled with the traditional way of doing the loop stitch then this method may be for you. Instead of forming loops on the back of the row, with this method the loops are formed in the front. You can create loops on one side of the work by alternating a row of loops and a row of regular single crochet (or any other stitch) Or have them on both sides by making loops in every row. Crochet inspiration.

item.title: Sleeve Scarf 101: The Easy Way to Put It On
item.description:
If you’ve ever been confused by a sleeve scarf, this is for you. (I wish someone would've showed me this sooner.)
And this is just how easy it is to put your sweater scarf on...
1. Cross the right arm over the left arm. 2. Put your right arm in the now right sleeve. 3. Put your left arm in the now left sleeve. 4. Adjust to fit. 5. Do a little dance.
Grab the free pattern here! 👉
#knitting #sweaterscarf #cozyknits #handmadewardrobe #freeknittingpattern #knittingpattern #sleevescarf #chunkyknit

item.title: Crochet Knit-style Ribbing - Version 1
item.description:
Looks like knit, but it’s crochet! It’s also very stretchy and a simple ribbing pattern! It’s simply a two row repeat of Yarn-over slip stitches, and slip stitches in the back loops.
This can be made any length. Start with any number of chs. Ch1 does not count as st. ROW 1: Starting in 2nd ch from hook YoSlst in each ch. ROW 2: Ch1, turn, Slst in the back loops only of each st. ROW 3: Ch1, turn, YoSlst in each st. Repeat alternating ROWS 2 & 3 until desired length
item.content:encoded: Looks like knit, but it’s crochet! It’s also very stretchy and a simple ribbing pattern! It’s simply a two row repeat of Yarn-over slip stitches, and slip stitches in the back loops. This can be made any length. Start with any number of chs. Ch1 does not count as st. ROW 1: Starting in 2nd ch from hook YoSlst in each ch. ROW 2: Ch1, turn, Slst in the back loops only of each st. ROW 3: Ch1, turn, YoSlst in each st. Repeat alternating ROWS 2 & 3 until desired length

item.title:
Adding ribbing to a finished edge doesn’t have to flare out or stretch weirdly.
The key is attaching it evenly as you g
item.description:
Adding ribbing to a finished edge doesn’t have to flare out or stretch weirdly.
The key is attaching it evenly as you go — working a sc2tog into the last st of the ribbing and the next st of the body stitch and slip stitching evenly so it lays flat and stays clean.
This method works beautifully for collars, hems, and sleeve cuffs when the body is already complete.
💾 Save this so you can reference it on your next garment project.
Have you ever struggled with ribbing flaring out?

item.description:
Cardboard Loom Woven Stocking with @yarnspirations #ad
Using cardboard and yarn to create this magical hand woven stocking!
I cut notches around the top and bottom of a cardboard stocking shape, wrapped the yarn around the tabs, and wove the coziest stocking. After weaving, you just slide it off the loom and stitch two pieces together with a blanket stitch.
